reason_matches.note: PREREG C-3 predicted the reason would be the IFF-equivalence, taken from the reference corpus. The respondent declines the iff and gives a more careful reason. So this is not the predicted reason -- and it is a BETTER one, which the scoring has to say rather than hide behind a matched verdict.

reason_better.note: PREREG section 5 says a correct verdict with a wrong reason is a wrong answer with a lucky verdict. It did not anticipate a reason that is DIFFERENT FROM THE PREDICTED ONE AND BETTER: the respondent declines the iff-equivalence that my prediction asserted, having taken it from the reference corpus. Scoring that as a lucky verdict would mark a respondent down for correcting me. So the rule needs a third case -- reason different and better, which fails the PREDICTION and not the response -- and this field records which way it was resolved rather than leaving the harness to pick the flattering reading.
